newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House subcommittee to hold April CEA hearings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House subcommittee to hold April CEA hearings.

text.p: A U.S. House agriculture subcommittee will hold hearings April 15 to 17 on proposed amendments to the Commodity Exchange Act, Representative Thomas Ewing, an Illinois Republican, said.
Ewing, who is chairman of the House subcommittee on risk management and specialty crops, told reporters the witness list for the hearings would be finalized shortly.
He said U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan would be invited to testify because of his role in the President's working group on financial markets.
Ewing, after addressing the Futures Industry Association's (FIA) annual conference here, said he hoped to have a House floor vote on a version of the bill this year.
However, he said more work needed to be done to hammer out the details of CEA reform.
He also said some of the criticism of current CEA reform legislation is "just unfounded."
"Much has recently been said alleging that Congress's legislative efforts to reform the Commodity Exchange Act will result in a savings-and-loan crisis or another Barings situation," he said.
Ewing said the Commodity Futures Trading Commission has taken the view that changes in the act, which regulates U.S. futures trading, could undermine provisions against fraud and manipulation.
"I am not convinced that all of what has been said is entirely accurate," he said. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
